title: Wine Wimsey Extras · Oct 24
subtitle: 4 extra feed posts from the inbox (all 4 new items, oldest first, quotes word for word), all as The Hot Mess · captions: 2 SEE MORE, 2 SHORT · wine glass in 3 of 4 · retake on #13 (removed an unrequested cat)

posts.quote: We didn’t keep begging our parents for new toys. We knew money was tight, so we took really good care of the few nice things we had.
posts.caption: My mother still has a tin truck from 1971 with one dented fender and a repaired bumper. It sits on a shelf like a trophy. We got one new thing a year, at Christmas, and guarded it like it held the deed to the house. I once cried over a scratched marble. A real cry. Last week I found that truck in a box in her spare room, wrapped in a dish towel, and I stood there longer than I'd like to admit. Nobody in that house was sentimental on purpose. We just had nothing to waste.
posts.first: My brother lost the pull string off his wooden dog in 1974 and my father spent a whole Sunday fixing it with a bobby pin and a rubber band. It still rolls. My brother is sixty now and checks it every time he visits. Nobody has ever said a word about it.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a wistful woman sitting cross-legged on the floor of a spare bedroom holding a small red toy pickup truck, with a worn teddy bear and a wooden pull-toy dog beside her, an open cardboard box and a glass of red wine on the rug. Text at the top reads: We didn’t keep begging our parents for new toys. We knew money was tight, so we took really good care of the few nice things we had.

posts.quote: I used to dress to impress. Now I dress so nothing pinches, tugs, digs in, or makes me hold my stomach in.
posts.caption: Nobody warns you that a waistband has opinions. Mine resigned at 2:15 on Thursday, in the middle of the cereal aisle, and I've been in elastic ever since. Best decision I've made all year.
posts.first: I own seven pairs of jeans and I wear one. The other six hang in the closet like relatives I'm still polite to. Last month I tried on the dark pair, sat down, and the button left the building. I put it in a drawer. We don't talk about it.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a smug woman standing in her bedroom with one hand on her hip, looking sideways at a bed where a pair of folded jeans, black high heels and a sparkly black dress are laid out, while an open closet behind her holds soft cardigans and stretchy pants. Text at the top reads: I used to dress to impress. Now I dress so nothing pinches, tugs, digs in, or makes me hold my stomach in.

posts.quote: Don’t wait for life to be perfect before you smile. Dance while dinner cooks, sing while you do the dishes, and remember that joy loves to show up on ordinary days.
posts.caption: My mother used to dance in the kitchen with oven mitts on and the radio turned up, and nobody was allowed to comment. I thought she'd lost her mind. Turns out she'd found the forty minutes where nobody needs anything from you.
posts.first: Tuesday I put the radio on while the chicken did its thing and caught myself mid-spin with a wooden spoon at 5:40. The neighbor was out taking her trash to the curb. She waved. I waved back with the spoon and kept going. Nobody was harmed and the chicken came out fine.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a joyful woman in yellow oven mitts dancing in a sunny kitchen, singing into a wooden spoon and holding a glass of red wine, with a steaming pot on the stove, a radio on the counter and dishes in the sink. Text at the top reads: Don’t wait for life to be perfect before you smile. Dance while dinner cooks, sing while you do the dishes, and remember that joy loves to show up on ordinary days.

posts.quote: Be the person who lights up someone’s life. Whether you use your sparkling personality or a blowtorch is totally your call.
posts.caption: I was handed a kitchen torch at a dinner party in 2019 and a lot of confidence came with it. I held it like I'd been trained. My sister-in-law asked if I was okay and I said I'd never been better, which was the problem. The creme brulee came out perfect. The tablecloth has a small scorch mark in one corner that we've agreed is part of the pattern. I've been invited back every year since, and I'm told it's for the company. Nobody has offered me the torch again, which I take as respect.
posts.first: I bought my own torch the next week. It lives in the drawer with the batteries and the takeout menus, and I take it out about twice a year. Last time my neighbor asked to borrow it and I said I'd have to check my schedule. She laughed. I wasn't joking.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a grinning woman on a back porch at dusk under string lights, holding a small kitchen torch in one hand and a lit sparkler in the other, with a tray of creme brulee and a glass of red wine on the table in front of her. Text at the top reads: Be the person who lights up someone’s life. Whether you use your sparkling personality or a blowtorch is totally your call.
